summary: Azerbaijan's official electronic visa portal says foreigners and stateless persons can apply directly through the portal for a single-entry visa valid for a 30-day stay. The standard e-Visa is issued within 3 working days; the fee is USD 20, plus a USD 9 service fee. Azerbaijan's Foreign Ministry lists the countries with which a visa-free regime applies under bilateral agreements, and the countries whose ordinary passport holders Azerbaijan exempts from visas unilaterally for a set period.

tips.text: The UK government's travel advice says anyone who has previously visited certain areas in south-western Azerbaijan, including the town of Khankendi, without the permission of the Azerbaijani authorities could be denied entry, and that you should contact the nearest embassy or consulate of Azerbaijan before you travel. It says the border with Armenia remains closed.

Canada's travel advice says that, due to the extension of COVID-19 border measures since 2020, all land border crossings are closed except for freight, and that Canadian passport holders can only enter Azerbaijan by air. The UK government says entry via a land or sea border is restricted and that if you want to leave Azerbaijan by road, you need permission from the authorities.

The UK government's travel advice says that if you're staying in Azerbaijan for longer than 15 days, you must register with the State Migration Service online or in person, and that if you do not register you will have to pay a fine before you are able to leave. Hotels often provide this service for their guests, but you must do it yourself if you are staying in an apartment or private residence.
The UK government's travel advice says you can apply and pay for a visa from the ASAN Visa (e-visa) service, the Republic of Azerbaijan Official Electronic Visa Portal at evisa.gov.az.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Azerbaijan?
faq.answer: Azerbaijan's official electronic visa portal publishes a list of countries eligible for the e-Visa, a single-entry visa valid for a 30-day stay that is applied for directly through the portal. Azerbaijan's Foreign Ministry lists the countries with which a visa-free regime applies under bilateral agreements, and the countries whose ordinary passport holders Azerbaijan exempts from visas unilaterally for a set period.

faq.question: How fast is the ASAN e-Visa?
faq.answer: The standard e-Visa is issued within 3 working days, and the urgent e-Visa within 3 hours, regardless of holidays and non-working days. The portal says to apply at least 3 working days before your planned arrival. The e-Visa is a single-entry visa valid for a 30-day stay.

faq.question: Can I enter Azerbaijan if I have been to Armenia?
faq.answer: The UK government's travel advice says anyone who has previously visited certain areas in south-western Azerbaijan, including the town of Khankendi, without the permission of the Azerbaijani authorities could be denied entry, and that you should contact the nearest embassy or consulate of Azerbaijan before you travel. No official source we could read says how a visit to Armenia itself is treated at the border.

faq.question: Can I cross into Azerbaijan by land?
faq.answer: Canada's travel advice says that, due to the extension of COVID-19 border measures since 2020, all land border crossings are closed except for freight, and that Canadian passport holders can only enter Azerbaijan by air. The UK government says the land borders between Iran and Azerbaijan, and Georgia and Azerbaijan, are temporarily closed.

faq.question: Do I need to register my stay in Azerbaijan?
faq.answer: The UK government's travel advice says that if you're staying in Azerbaijan for longer than 15 days, you must register with the State Migration Service online or in person, and that if you do not register you will have to pay a fine before you are able to leave. It says hotels often provide this service for their guests, but you must do it yourself if you are staying in an apartment or private residence.

entryRequirements.customs.currencyLimits.text: Resident and non-resident physical and legal persons are entitled to bring the foreign currency to the Republic of Azerbaijan without any restrictions, by complying with customs procedures.

Resident and non-resident physical and legal persons are entitled to take out of the Republic of Azerbaijan the foreign currency up to the equivalent of USD 10,000 (ten thousand) in cash via oral declaration to the customs authorities.

Resident and non-resident physical and legal persons can take out of the Republic of Azerbaijan the foreign currency equivalent from USD 10,000 (ten thousand) to USD 50,000 (fifty thousand) US dollars in cash, by submitting to the customs authority the customs documents and written declaration certifying the bringing of that amount to the Republic of Azerbaijan before in cash form.

In all other cases, except for abovementioned cases, the foreign currency can be taken out of the Republic of Azerbaijan by physical and legal persons by means of transfer via authorized banks and national postal operators.

countryFacts.safety.text: Crime levels in Baku are generally low.

The FCDO advises against all travel to within 5km of the border with Armenia, due to tensions between Azerbaijan and Armenia. Note that this does not include the border of Azerbaijan’s Nakhchivan exclave with Armenia.
The districts (‘rayons’) of Kelbajar, Lachin, Qubadli, Zengilan, Jabrayil, Fuzuli, Khojavand, Shusha, Khojali, Khankendi, Aghdam and Tartar
You should follow Azerbaijani national government and local authorities’ advice in areas that have not been cleared of mines or unexploded ordnance.

countryFacts.driving.text: Convention on Road Traffic Vienna, 8 November 1968
You’ll need to have both the 1968 version of the international driving permit (IDP) and your UK driving licence with you in the car.
After one month, you will need an Azerbaijani driving licence issued through the ASAN Service Offices.
